questions.question: Which company originally created the Android operating system before Google acquired it in 2005?
questions.explanation: Android Inc. was founded in Palo Alto, California in 2003 by Andy Rubin, Rich Miner, Nick Sears, and Chris White before Google bought it.
questions.funFact: Andy Rubin originally developed Android as an OS for digital cameras, not smartphones!

questions.question: What does the 'GPT' in ChatGPT stand for?
questions.explanation: GPT stands for Generative Pre-trained Transformer, based on the Transformer architecture introduced by Google researchers in 2017.
questions.funFact: The breakthrough 'Attention Is All You Need' paper revolutionized modern AI in just 11 pages!

questions.question: What was the very first video ever uploaded to YouTube in April 2005?
questions.explanation: 'Me at the zoo' was uploaded by YouTube co-founder Jawed Karim at the San Diego Zoo on April 23, 2005.
questions.funFact: The video is only 19 seconds long and shows elephants in the background!

questions.question: Which programming language was originally called 'Oak' before being renamed?
questions.explanation: James Gosling named Java 'Oak' after an oak tree outside his office window at Sun Microsystems.
questions.funFact: It was renamed to Java after the popular Indonesian coffee consumed by the development team!

questions.question: In what year did the legendary chess AI 'Deep Blue' defeat World Champion Garry Kasparov?
questions.explanation: IBM's Deep Blue defeated Garry Kasparov in a 6-game match in May 1997, marking a milestone in artificial intelligence history.
questions.funFact: Kasparov initially accused IBM of cheating by having a human grandmaster secretly intervene!

questions.question: Who invented the World Wide Web while working at CERN in 1989?
questions.explanation: Tim Berners-Lee proposed a system of linked hypertext documents at CERN, and the first website went live in 1991.
questions.funFact: CERN made the web technology free to use in 1993.

questions.question: Who unveiled the first iPhone in January 2007?
questions.explanation: Steve Jobs introduced the iPhone at Macworld 2007, calling it a widescreen iPod, a phone and an internet communicator.
questions.funFact: The first iPhone did not have an App Store.

questions.question: Who created the Linux kernel in 1991?
questions.explanation: Finnish student Linus Torvalds began Linux as a hobby project, and it now powers Android, servers and supercomputers.
questions.funFact: Linux's mascot is a penguin named Tux.

questions.question: The Python programming language is named after what?
questions.explanation: Guido van Rossum named Python after the British comedy show Monty Python's Flying Circus.
questions.funFact: Python's first version was released in 1991.

questions.question: What was the first literal 'computer bug' found in 1947?
options: A moth in a Harvard Mark II relay
A beetle in a tape drive
questions.explanation: Operators found a moth stuck in a relay of the Harvard Mark II and taped it into the logbook, and the term 'debugging' was popularised by Grace Hopper's team.
questions.funFact: The moth is preserved at the Smithsonian.

questions.question: Which early computer, completed in 1945, is often called the first general-purpose electronic computer?
questions.explanation: ENIAC was built at the University of Pennsylvania and occupied a room, using thousands of vacuum tubes.
questions.funFact: It weighed about 30 tons.

questions.question: What is the Turing Test, proposed by Alan Turing in 1950, designed to test?
options: Whether a machine can imitate human conversation
questions.explanation: Turing's imitation game asks whether a human judge can tell a machine from a person in text conversation.
questions.funFact: Turing also helped break the Enigma code in WWII.

questions.question: Who coined the term 'artificial intelligence' at the 1956 Dartmouth workshop?
questions.explanation: John McCarthy used the term in the proposal for the Dartmouth Summer Research Project on Artificial Intelligence.
questions.funFact: McCarthy also invented the Lisp programming language.

questions.question: In 2016, Google DeepMind's AlphaGo defeated which world-class Go player?
questions.explanation: AlphaGo beat Lee Sedol 4 games to 1 in Seoul, a milestone since Go is far more complex than chess.
questions.funFact: Its famous 'Move 37' shocked experts.

questions.question: Which company acquired the AI lab DeepMind in 2014?
questions.explanation: Google acquired DeepMind, founded in London in 2010, in 2014 for a reported price of around $500 million.
questions.funFact: DeepMind's co-founder Demis Hassabis later shared a Nobel Prize.

questions.question: How quickly did ChatGPT reach 1 million users after launching in November 2022?
questions.explanation: ChatGPT launched on 30 November 2022 and hit 1 million users in about five days.
questions.funFact: It was one of the fastest-growing consumer apps ever.

questions.question: In which year was OpenAI founded?
questions.explanation: OpenAI was founded in December 2015 as a non-profit AI research lab.
questions.funFact: Co-founders included Sam Altman and Elon Musk.

questions.question: Which AI company, founded in 2021 by former OpenAI researchers including Dario and Daniela Amodei, makes Claude?
questions.explanation: Anthropic is an AI safety company that builds the Claude family of AI models.
questions.funFact: Anthropic was founded by a group of former OpenAI researchers with a focus on AI safety.

questions.question: What does Moore's Law predict?
options: Transistors on a chip double roughly every two years
questions.explanation: Gordon Moore observed in 1965 that chip transistor counts grow exponentially, and the pace was later stated as doubling about every two years.
questions.funFact: Moore co-founded Intel.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of Bitcoin that can ever exist?
questions.explanation: Bitcoin's code caps supply at 21 million coins, making it scarce by design.
questions.funFact: Its creator, Satoshi Nakamoto, has never been definitively identified.

questions.question: What does 'HTTP' stand for?
questions.explanation: HTTP is the protocol web browsers use to request pages from servers.
questions.funFact: HTTPS adds encryption for security.

questions.question: What does RAM stand for in computers?
questions.explanation: RAM is fast, temporary memory that a computer uses for running programs.
questions.funFact: Data in RAM is lost when power is turned off.

questions.question: Who sent the first network email in 1971 and popularised the '@' symbol?
questions.explanation: Ray Tomlinson used the @ symbol to separate the user name from the host on ARPANET.
questions.funFact: He couldn't remember the content of the first email.

questions.question: Why was the QWERTY keyboard layout designed?
questions.explanation: Christopher Latham Sholes arranged keys to keep commonly paired letters apart, reducing jamming on early typewriters.
questions.funFact: The layout survived long after typewriters disappeared.

questions.question: Who invented the first computer mouse in the 1960s?
questions.explanation: Douglas Engelbart and Bill English built the first mouse prototype at Stanford Research Institute.
questions.funFact: The first mouse was made of wood.

questions.question: In which year was Google Chrome launched?
questions.explanation: Google launched the Chrome browser in September 2008.
questions.funFact: It is now the world's most-used browser.

questions.question: How much free storage did Gmail offer when it launched on 1 April 2004?
questions.explanation: Gmail's 1 GB of free storage was massive compared with rivals' few megabytes, and many people thought it was an April Fools joke.
questions.funFact: It was invite-only at first.

questions.question: In July 2023, Twitter was rebranded as what?
questions.explanation: Elon Musk's company changed the Twitter name and logo to X in July 2023.
questions.funFact: Twitter was originally styled as 'twttr'.

questions.question: Which organisation manages India's Unified Payments Interface (UPI), launched in 2016?
questions.explanation: The National Payments Corporation of India launched UPI in 2016, enabling instant bank transfers with a phone.
questions.funFact: India became the world leader in real-time digital payments.

questions.question: Which was India's first indigenous supercomputer series, developed by C-DAC in 1991 under Vijay Bhatkar?
questions.explanation: PARAM 8000 was built after India was denied a foreign supercomputer.
questions.funFact: 'Param' means 'supreme' in Sanskrit.

questions.question: Which Indian city is known as the 'Silicon Valley of India'?
questions.explanation: Bengaluru is home to a huge number of IT firms and startups, and hosts many global tech centres.
questions.funFact: It is also home to ISRO's headquarters.

questions.question: In which year did Sundar Pichai become CEO of Google?
questions.explanation: Pichai became Google's CEO in 2015 and CEO of parent company Alphabet in 2019.
questions.funFact: He joined Google in 2004 and helped launch Chrome.

questions.question: Satya Nadella, the CEO of Microsoft since 2014, was born in which Indian city?
questions.explanation: Nadella was born in Hyderabad and studied at Manipal before moving to the US.
questions.funFact: He followed Steve Ballmer as CEO.

questions.question: Geoffrey Hinton, the 'Godfather of AI', won the Nobel Prize in which field in 2024?
questions.explanation: Hinton shared the 2024 Nobel Prize in Physics with John Hopfield for work on artificial neural networks.
questions.funFact: Hinton left Google in 2023 to speak about AI's risks.

questions.question: What does DeepMind's AlphaFold predict?
questions.explanation: AlphaFold can predict protein structures from amino-acid sequences, helping drug discovery and biology.
questions.funFact: Its creators shared the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

questions.question: In which year did Apple introduce Siri on the iPhone 4S?
questions.explanation: Siri came out in October 2011 as the first mainstream voice assistant on a smartphone.
questions.funFact: Siri began as a separate app before Apple bought it.

questions.question: Which company launched the Echo smart speaker with Alexa in 2014?
questions.explanation: Amazon's Echo introduced the Alexa voice assistant in late 2014.
questions.funFact: The name Alexa was inspired by the Library of Alexandria.

questions.question: IBM's Watson AI famously won which TV quiz show in 2011?
options: Who Wants to Be a Millionaire
questions.explanation: Watson defeated champions Ken Jennings and Brad Rutter on Jeopardy!
questions.funFact: Watson was named after IBM's founder, Thomas J. Watson.

questions.question: What does CAPTCHA stand for?
options: Completely Automated Public Turing test to tell Computers and Humans Apart
questions.explanation: CAPTCHA is designed to tell humans from bots with challenges only humans could easily solve.
questions.funFact: It's basically a reverse Turing test.

questions.question: What does 'Wi-Fi' actually stand for?
questions.explanation: 'Wireless Fidelity' is a popular myth; the name was made up by a branding firm.
questions.funFact: The term was created in 1999.

questions.question: Bluetooth is named after a medieval king of which country?
questions.explanation: The technology is named after King Harald Bluetooth of Denmark, who united tribes, as Bluetooth unites devices.
questions.funFact: The Bluetooth logo combines Harald's initials in Viking runes.

questions.question: Who is often called the 'father of the computer' for designing the Analytical Engine?
questions.explanation: Charles Babbage designed the mechanical Analytical Engine in the 1830s, a concept ahead of its time.
questions.funFact: It was never fully built during his life.

questions.question: Who is often considered the world's first computer programmer?
questions.explanation: Ada Lovelace wrote an algorithm for Babbage's Analytical Engine in the 1840s.
questions.funFact: She was the daughter of the poet Lord Byron.

questions.question: Which company made the first smartphone, the 'Simon' in 1994?
questions.explanation: The IBM Simon Personal Communicator had a touchscreen and could send emails and faxes.
questions.funFact: It came about 13 years before the iPhone.

questions.question: Which research lab developed the Alto computer, which inspired graphical user interfaces?
questions.explanation: Xerox PARC's Alto pioneered windows, icons and the mouse, ideas later adopted by Apple and Microsoft.
questions.funFact: Steve Jobs visited PARC in 1979.

questions.question: In AI, what is a 'hallucination'?
options: When a model confidently generates false information
When a model repeats a word
questions.explanation: AI hallucinations are outputs that sound plausible but are made up or incorrect.
questions.funFact: That's why AI answers should be verified.

questions.question: Who created the Git version-control system in 2005?
questions.explanation: Torvalds built Git in a few weeks to manage the Linux kernel's development.
questions.funFact: Torvalds joked that he names his projects after himself, since 'git' is British slang for an unpleasant person.

questions.question: How much did Microsoft pay to acquire GitHub in 2018?
questions.explanation: Microsoft bought GitHub for about $7.5 billion in stock.
questions.funFact: GitHub hosts over 100 million developers.

questions.question: Which programming language does Google's Flutter framework use?
questions.explanation: Flutter, an open-source UI toolkit, uses Dart to build apps for mobile, web and desktop from one codebase.
questions.funFact: Flutter was first released in 2017.

questions.question: Which company introduced the 'GPU' with the GeForce 256 in 1999?
questions.explanation: Nvidia marketed the GeForce 256 as the world's first GPU.
questions.funFact: GPUs later became the engines of the AI boom.
